translation: `Target` defines the following proposition (it names the statement without asserting or proving it): For all types `X` and `Y`, assuming `X` is nonempty (has at least one element), and for every system `N` of type `S1 X Y`—consisting of a finite type of nodes/components `A1`, a local state type `A3 n` for each node `n` (not required to be finite), an initial global state `a4` assigning an element of `A3 n` to each node `n`, a local transition function `a5` computing the next local state of each node `n` from the full current global state and an input in `X`, and an output function `a6` mapping a global state to `Y`—there exists a system `N'` of type `S1 X Y` such that all three of the following hold: (1) `N'` has at least one node (`N'.A1` is nonempty), and for every pair of nodes `m` and `n` of `N'` (including `m = n`), there is a directed chain of length at least 1 (`m = c_0, c_1, ..., c_k = n` with `k >= 1`) where at each step `i`, node `c_{i+1}`'s transition function depends on node `c_i`—meaning there exist two global states `σ` and `σ'` of `N'` (not required to be reachable from `N'`'s initial state) that agree at every node other than `c_i`, together with an input `x` in `X`, such that `N'.a5 c_{i+1} σ x ≠ N'.a5 c_{i+1} σ' x` (in particular, every node must lie on a directed cycle of length at least 1, so a 1-node `N'` must have a self-dependency); (2) the number of nodes of `N'` equals the number of nodes of `N` plus 1 (`Fintype.card N'.A1 = Fintype.card N.A1 + 1`); and (3) `N'` and `N` produce the same output in `Y` on every finite input list `xs : List X` (including the empty list), where the output on `xs` is obtained by starting from the initial global state, updating all nodes simultaneously step-by-step left-to-right across the elements of `xs`, and applying the output function. Neither `X` nor `Y` is required to be finite, `N` is not required to have any nodes (it may have 0 nodes), and `N'` is not required to reuse the node type, local state types, or internal state space of `N`.

divergences.description: In the formalization, causal dependence (D7/D8) is evaluated over all global states—including states unreachable from the initial state a4—and N' is unrestricted in its choice of local state types A3. Consequently, the feedback loops guaranteed by D11 need not be active on any reachable execution from a4 (and D11 guarantees directed closed walks between every pair of units, not necessarily simple cycles).

The formal model S1 restricts 'every system' to deterministic, synchronous, discrete-time systems with finitely many units, a fixed initial state, and state-only (Moore-type) outputs; this is an idealization implicit in 'the author's model' rather than explicitly spelled out in the description.

In comparing TARGET to the passages, the description omits noting that D11 (every unit mutually reachable from every unit) is structurally stronger than bare recurrence in premise P2 ([P-D53]), and that the Nonempty X hypothesis (stated in the description of TARGET) is not explicitly stated in the passages (where nonempty inputs are tacit). Also, Appendix A ([P-D57]) informally writes a static input-output mapping x → F(x), though it indeed does not specify a finite-input-history machine model.

judgement.summary: The Lean statement Target matches the author's description in all quantifiers, hypotheses, and conclusions, and the description accurately characterizes premise P2, [P-D52b], and Appendix A. The only caveats are minor modeling and presentational details—most notably that D7/D11 checks counterfactual dependence over all (possibly unreachable) global states with unconstrained local state spaces in N'.
